title: Mixedness of the direct images over a relative affine curve
statement:
Fix the coefficient and weight conventions of
[def-weil-punctual-weights]. Let $h:U_0\to Y_0$ be a
smooth separated morphism
between separated finite-type
$k_0$-schemes, with every nonempty geometric fiber a smooth affine curve,
and let $\mathcal F$ be a
lisse
$\Qlb$-Weil sheaf that is
punctually $\iota$-pure of weight
$w$. Then for every $i$ there is a real number $u_i$ such that
$R^ih_!\mathcal F$ is
$\iota$-mixed of weights at most
$u_i$.

proof.text: Choose $b=\iota^{-1}(q^{-w/2})\in\Qlb^\times$ and put $\mathcal F^0=\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal B_b$ and $\mathcal E=\mathcal F^0\oplus(\mathcal F^0)^\vee$, as in [def-wf-normalized-real-envelope]. This choice is allowed because the fixed $\iota$ is an isomorphism and $q^{-w/2}>0$. Since $q>1$, $2\log_q|\iota(b)|=-w$. By [lem-wf-constant-twist-weight], $\mathcal F^0$ is punctually pure of weight zero. It is lisse: its underlying geometric sheaf is the tensor of the lisse sheaf $\mathcal F$ with a constant one-dimensional sheaf. By [lem-tw-dual-negation], $(\mathcal F^0)^\vee$ is also pure of weight zero. The Frobenius matrix of the direct sum is block diagonal, so its characteristic polynomial is the product of the two characteristic polynomials; all eigenvalues of $\mathcal E$ therefore have modulus one. Thus $\mathcal E$ is pure of weight zero. Finally [lem-wf-envelope-real] gives both lissity and $\iota$-reality of $\mathcal E$.

source.place: paragraph 1, normalization and the real envelope; purity made explicit

proof.text: We check the constructible domain before applying the real-sheaf theorem. All schemes are separated and of finite type over $k_0$, and $h$ is separated and of finite type; $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$. Regard $\mathcal E$ in degree zero. In the common-stage construction [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], its underlying complex is represented at a finite field $E/\Ql$ by an integral constructible complex $K$. The theorem [lem-sf-integral-compact-support-constructible] applies to $K$ and $h$ and puts its integral compact-support image in $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$. Rationalization and the common-stage formula in the cited definition therefore put $Rh_!\mathcal E$ in $D^b_c(Y,\Qlb)$. This uses completed integral coefficients, followed by rationalization, not discrete non-torsion coefficients on the etale site. The lift [prop-weil-operations] equips this output with its Weil structure and makes its morphisms Frobenius compatible. By [prop-constructible-truncations], its cohomology $\mathcal G_i=\mathcal H^i(Rh_!\mathcal E)$ is in the constructible heart and inherits that structure. Hence each $\mathcal G_i$ is a constructible $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf. The same reasoning applies to $Rh_!\mathcal F$ and $Rh_!\mathcal F^0$.

source.place: paragraph 1, constructible landing (replace the insufficient finiteness/base-change citation by the existing preservation theorem)

proof.text: The morphism $h$ satisfies precisely the hypotheses of [lem-zl-relative-envelope-factor-reality]: it is smooth and separated between separated finite-type schemes with every nonempty geometric fiber an affine curve. Step 1 supplies its other three hypotheses: $\mathcal E$ is lisse, real and pure of weight zero. That lemma gives $\iota$-reality of $\mathcal G_i$ for every $i$. The scheme $Y_0$ is separated and of finite type over the finite field, and Step 2 supplies constructibility. Apply [thm-zl-real-mixed-by-curves] to obtain a finite mixed filtration of $\mathcal G_i$. Choose a real upper bound $v_i$ for its finitely many pure-quotient weights; when the filtration is empty take $v_i=0$.

source.place: paragraphs 1-2, reality of the relative factors and mixedness on the base

proof.text: Write $a:\mathcal F^0\to\mathcal E$ and $p:\mathcal E\to\mathcal F^0$ for the inclusion and projection of the first summand, so $p\circ a=1$. Applying the functor $\mathcal H^i Rh_!$ gives maps whose composite is still the identity; these are maps of Weil sheaves by [prop-weil-operations] and the Frobenius-compatible cohomology functors [prop-constructible-truncations]. Consequently $R^ih_!\mathcal F^0$ is a retract, hence a Weil direct summand, of $\mathcal G_i$. Clause 3 of [lem-a1-mixed-direct-summand] gives a finite mixed filtration of $R^ih_!\mathcal F^0$ of weights at most $v_i$. This uses functoriality of the retraction and requires no exactness of $R^ih_!$.

The pullback to $U_0$ of the constant Weil line $\mathcal B_b$ on $Y_0$ is the constant Weil line with the same scalar, since both actions are $g\mapsto b^{\deg(g)}$. Apply [lem-wf-constant-twist-cohomology] to $h$, $\mathcal F$ and this line. Its hypotheses hold: $h$ is separated of finite type, both schemes are separated of finite type, and $\mathcal F$ in degree zero is constructible. It gives a Frobenius-compatible isomorphism $Rh_!\mathcal F^0\cong Rh_!\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal B_b$. The underlying geometric line is constant of rank one, so tensoring with it preserves kernels and images, and hence commutes with cohomology. In degree $i$ and then tensoring with its inverse line, this identifies
$$R^ih_!\mathcal F\cong (R^ih_!\mathcal F^0)\otimes\mathcal B_{b^{-1}}.$$
The cancellation of the two lines is Weil compatible: their Frobenius scalars multiply to $bb^{-1}=1$.

Tensor the finite filtration from Step 4 by $\mathcal B_{b^{-1}}$. This is exact, since the underlying geometric line is the constant one-dimensional coefficient sheaf; on underlying sheaves tensoring with it is isomorphic to the identity. Subsheaves and quotients therefore remain constructible, with their induced Weil structures. If a quotient was pure of weight $t$, then at a degree-$m$ closed point its Frobenius eigenvalues become $b^{-m}\alpha$ by [def-wf-constant-weil-twist]. Since $q_y=q^m$ and $|\iota(b^{-m})|=q^{mw/2}$, their moduli are $q_y^{t/2}q_y^{w/2}=q_y^{(t+w)/2}$. Thus this quotient is pure of weight $t+w$ by [def-weil-punctual-weights]. All these weights are at most $v_i+w$. Step 5 transports this filtration to $R^ih_!\mathcal F$, so $u_i=v_i+w$ works. Zero stalks impose no eigenvalue condition, and the zero sheaf has the empty filtration. No lissity of a direct image is used.

source.place: paragraph 3, exact untwisting and the weight calculation

Fix the coefficient and weight conventions of
[def-weil-punctual-weights]. Let $h:U_0\to Y_0$ be a
smooth separated morphism
between separated finite-type
$k_0$-schemes, with every nonempty geometric fiber a smooth affine curve,
and let $\mathcal F$ be a
lisse
$\Qlb$-Weil sheaf that is
punctually $\iota$-pure of weight
$w$. Then for every $i$ there is a real number $u_i$ such that
$R^ih_!\mathcal F$ is
$\iota$-mixed of weights at most

proof.text:
Normalize $\mathcal F$ as in
[def-wf-normalized-real-envelope]: put
$b=\iota^{-1}(q^{-w/2})$,
$\mathcal F^0=\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal B_b$, and
$\mathcal E=\mathcal F^0\oplus(\mathcal F^0)^\vee$.
It is lisse, pure of weight zero and real by
[lem-wf-envelope-real]. The relative factor calculation
[lem-zl-relative-envelope-factor-reality], which uses only the
proved curve estimate, shows that $R^ih_!\mathcal E$ is real for
every $i$. These are constructible sheaves: the finite-level
finiteness theorem [sbc-thm-finiteness-finite-type] supplies the
constructible landing hypotheses in the coefficient passage of
[thm-cbc-qbar].

Apply [thm-zl-real-mixed-by-curves] on $Y_0$, obtaining a
finite mixed filtration of $R^ih_!\mathcal E$.
Additivity makes $R^ih_!\mathcal F^0$ a direct summand, so it is
mixed by [lem-a1-mixed-direct-summand]. The constant-twist
projection formula [lem-wf-constant-twist-cohomology] identifies

$$
R^ih_!\mathcal F
\cong R^ih_!\mathcal F^0\otimes\mathcal B_{b^{-1}}.
$$

Tensoring the finite filtration with this rank-one sheaf is exact.
At a closed point of degree $m$, the twist multiplies each
eigenvalue by $b^{-m}$, of $\iota$-modulus $q^{mw/2}$, by
[def-wf-constant-weil-twist]. Thus every pure quotient of weight
$v$ becomes pure of weight $v+w$, including where its stalk is
zero. This gives the required finite mixed filtration without a
lissity assumption on the direct image. Its finitely many
weights have a maximum $u_i$; for the zero sheaf take any $u_i$.
